risks.note: Fluctuations in prices of steel, fuel, energy and other key inputs may increase project costs and adversely affect profitability, particularly where contracts do not provide adequate price escalation mechanisms.

Delays in land availability, work-front handover, statutory approvals, client clearances, material availability or other project-related dependencies may affect project schedules, costs and cash flows.
Delays in project certification, billing and collection of receivables may increase working capital requirements and place pressure on liquidity and timely execution of projects.
Shortages of skilled, semi-skilled and technical personnel, particularly during major shutdown and turnaround assignments, may affect project execution and timelines.

The industrial EPC, fabrication, construction and maintenance sectors remain highly competitive, with increased competition for large projects potentially resulting in pricing pressure and lower margins.

The transition towards cleaner energy sources and increasing emphasis on sustainability may alter investment patterns in conventional energy sectors, requiring the Company to continuously adapt its capabilities and service offerings.

Increasing dependence on digital systems and communication networks exposes the business to threats such as ransomware, phishing, data breaches and system disruptions, which may affect operations and information security.
Geopolitical tensions, global trade uncertainties, protectionist measures and volatility in commodity and energy prices may affect supply chains, project costs and overall investment activity.
